model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis represents the Co-occurrence Number on a logarithmic scale, featuring visible tick marks at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis represents ACC (%), plotted on a linear scale with visible tick marks ranging from 40 to 65 at intervals of 5. All six methods are represented by solid lines and demonstrate an overall upward trend across four distinct data points along the x-axis. The "Base" method is depicted by a black line with circular markers, starting at an ACC of approximately 38, rising to roughly 44 at the third data point, and remaining steady at 44 at the final point. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, increasing steadily from approximately 40 to 48. The "IKE" method uses a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, showing a gradual increase from roughly 43 to 49.5. The "MEND" method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at approximately 44.5, rising to 54 at the third data point, and ending at 56.5. The "MEMIT" method is indicated by a purple line with pentagon markers, beginning at roughly 43.5, increasing to 51 at the second data point, and concluding at 54.5. Finally, the "ROME" method is plotted with a green line and square markers, starting at approximately 51 and consistently increasing to reach the highest overall value of roughly 66 at the final data point.
